```{r}
# calling in the gaussian_sizeweight function
gaussian_sizeweight <- function(w, species_params, w_opt, sigma, ...) {
  exp(-0.5 * ((log(w) - log(w_opt)) / sigma)^2)
}
```

Read in params object
```{r}

# ── Factual model (Stage 2) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
params <- readRDS(if (file.exists("Ess_data/params_stage2_AUTO.RDS"))
                    "Ess_data/params_stage2_AUTO.RDS" else
                    "Ess_data/params_stage2_factual.RDS")

# ── Effort: FACTUAL = seal increase 1978->2024; COUNTERFACTUAL = seals constant ─
eff <- read.csv("Ess_data/effort_gear_with_seals.csv")
gear_cols <- c("Bottom_Trawl","Fixed_Gear","Small_Mesh","Pelagic","Seals")
effort_factual <- as.matrix(eff[eff$Year %in% 1978:2024, gear_cols])
rownames(effort_factual) <- eff$Year[eff$Year %in% 1978:2024]

# The ONE counterfactual: NO seal increase — seal effort HELD CONSTANT at the 1978
# level for all years; fishing identical to factual. (Seal catchability is baked into
# `params`, so holding effort low keeps seal predation at its 1978 strength throughout.)
effort_counter <- effort_factual
effort_counter[, "Seals"] <- effort_factual[1, "Seals"]

# Reference factual run (no randomisation) for relative plots
sim0 <- project(params, effort = effort_factual)
plotlyBiomass(sim0)

# Quick test: one randomised-web run
rand_params <- randomize_interaction_matrix(params)
sim1 <- project(rand_params, effort = effort_factual)
plot(sim1, time_range = c(1978:2024))
plotBiomassRelative(sim1, sim0)

# ── ENSEMBLE: factual vs counterfactual over randomised food webs ─────────────
# Structural-uncertainty robustness test: randomize_interaction_matrix() multiplies each
# existing interaction-matrix entry AND each seal catchability by lognormal noise (SD =
# sd_web) - scaling existing link STRENGTHS (topology preserved, zeros stay zero) and
# perturbing seal predation the same way. Projected from the calibrated 1978 state (a
# transient hindcast, not equilibrium). PAIRED: same web under both scenarios, so the
# per-web difference isolates the seal effect and cancels the perturbation drift =>
# base conclusions on the paired difference / fraction of webs, not the ribbon spread.
# sd_web = 0.1 = primary (~10% CV/link, realistic); 0.2 = stronger stress test (below).
n_sims <- 1000; sd_web <- 0.1

# CACHE GUARD: the n=1000 paired ensemble is the expensive step (~15 min). Run it
# ONCE; every later knit reads the saved RDS in seconds. To regenerate after changing
# `params`, set force_resim <- TRUE before this chunk (or delete the two RDS files).
cache_f <- "Ess_Output/sims_factual.RDS"   # seal increase (factual)
cache_c <- "Ess_Output/sims_counter.RDS"   # seals constant (counterfactual)
if (file.exists(cache_f) && file.exists(cache_c) && !exists("force_resim")) {
  sims_factual <- readRDS(cache_f)
  sims_counter <- readRDS(cache_c)
  cat(sprintf("Loaded cached ensemble: %d paired members (set force_resim<-TRUE to rerun)\n",
              length(sims_factual)))
} else {
  paired <- run_paired_sims(params, n_sims = n_sims, sd = sd_web,
                            effort_factual = effort_factual,
                            effort_counter = effort_counter, seed = 42)
  sims_factual <- paired$factual
  sims_counter <- paired$counter

  # Keep only COMPLETE pairs (drop index i if either scenario failed) so the two lists
  # stay aligned & indexable: factual[[k]] and counter[[k]] are the SAME web.
  ok <- which(!vapply(sims_factual, is.null, logical(1)) &
              !vapply(sims_counter, is.null, logical(1)))
  sims_factual <- sims_factual[ok]; sims_counter <- sims_counter[ok]
  cat(sprintf("Kept %d / %d complete paired ensemble members\n", length(ok), n_sims))

  # Save sim outputs (complete-pair filtered) for downstream use (04_Indicators)
  saveRDS(sims_factual, cache_f)
  saveRDS(sims_counter, cache_c)
}

# Aliases for the downstream figure code (scen2 = factual/with seal increase;
# scen1 = counterfactual/no seal increase) — now PAIRED by index
sims_scen2 <- sims_factual
sims_scen1 <- sims_counter


# Save sim outputs (complete-pair filtered) for downstream use (04_Indicators)
saveRDS(sims_factual, "Ess_Output/sims_factual.RDS")   # seal increase (factual)
saveRDS(sims_counter, "Ess_Output/sims_counter.RDS")   # seals constant (counterfactual)
sims_factual <- readRDS("Ess_Output/sims_factual.RDS")
sims_counter <- readRDS("Ess_Output/sims_counter.RDS")


# Check results from first simulation
plot(sims_factual[[4]],time_range=c(1978:2024))

plotBiomassRelative(sims_factual[[4]],sim0)
```

## Paired robustness across the randomised-web ensemble

Because the ensemble is PAIRED (web `k` is run under both scenarios), we can take the
per-web difference and ask: across the randomised food webs, does removing the seal
increase let cod / groundfish recover MORE? This is a far stronger robustness claim
than overlapping ribbons — it isolates the seal effect on identical structure.

The Stage-2 model is an intentional transient relaxation from the calibrated 1978
reference, not an equilibrium run; attribution therefore rests on this paired
factual − counterfactual difference, which cancels the large baseline reorganization
common to both scenarios rather than on either absolute trajectory.

```{r paired-robustness}

# Per-species terminal (2024) biomass above each species' survey cutoff (kt)
cutoff <- species_params(params)$biomass_cutoff; cutoff[is.na(cutoff)] <- 0
sppx   <- species_params(params)$species
term_bio <- function(sim, yr = 2024) {
  n <- sim@n[as.character(yr), , ]
  sapply(seq_along(sppx), function(j)
    sum(n[j, params@w >= cutoff[j]] * (params@w * params@dw)[params@w >= cutoff[j]])) / 1e9
}

# Build the PAIRED data frame (web k: factual vs counterfactual terminal biomass)
pair_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sims_factual), function(k) {
  data.frame(web = k, species = sppx,
             factual = term_bio(sims_factual[[k]]),
             counter = term_bio(sims_counter[[k]]))
}))
pair_df$log_ratio <- log(pmax(pair_df$counter, 1e-9) / pmax(pair_df$factual, 1e-9))

# Robustness summary: % of webs where the species recovers MORE without the seal increase
robust <- pair_df |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(pct_recover_more_no_seal = round(100 * mean(counter > factual), 1),
            median_cf_over_factual   = round(median(counter / pmax(factual, 1e-9)), 2),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(pct_recover_more_no_seal))
print(as.data.frame(robust))
cat(sprintf("\nCod recovery suppressed by the seal increase in %.1f%% of %d webs\n",
            robust$pct_recover_more_no_seal[robust$species == "Atlantic Cod"],
            length(sims_factual)))

# Figure A — paired log-ratio distribution across webs (groundfish); >0 = seal increase
# suppressed recovery. Boxplots summarise the per-web paired differences.
gf <- c("Atlantic Cod","Haddock","Pollock","White Hake","Silver Hake",
        "Redfish Unseparated","American Plaice","Yellowtail Flounder","Witch Flounder")
pA <- ggplot(filter(pair_df, species %in% gf),
             aes(x = factor(species, levels = rev(gf)), y = log_ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_violin(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.4, colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.size = 0.4) +
  coord_flip() + theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "log( counterfactual / factual )  terminal biomass")
ggsave(paste0(save_dir, "scenario_paired_recovery_logratio.jpeg"), pA, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 200)
pA

# Figure B — cod: factual vs counterfactual 2024 biomass, each point a food web
cod <- filter(pair_df, species == "Atlantic Cod")
pB <- ggplot(cod, aes(factual, counter)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "purple") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, colour = "firebrick") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  labs(x = "Cod 2024 biomass — FACTUAL (seal increase), kt",
       y = "Cod 2024 biomass — COUNTERFACTUAL (seals constant), kt")
ggsave(paste0(save_dir, "scenario_paired_cod_scatter.jpeg"), pB, width = 6.5, height = 6, dpi = 200)
pB

# INTERPRETATION (kept as comments; no plot titles/captions per journal style):
# pA: per-species distribution across webs of log(counterfactual/factual) 2024 biomass;
#     > 0 = recovers MORE without the seal increase. Wholly-positive (e.g. Atlantic Cod)
#     = seal increase suppresses recovery in ~all webs.
# pB: cod factual vs counterfactual per web; points above the 1:1 line = counterfactual
#     cod > factual. Paired (same web both scenarios) => isolates the seal effect, robust
#     to food-web structural uncertainty. Time-series ribbons = 10-90% ensemble spread
#     (visual range, NOT a CI); formal claim = the paired fraction-of-webs.

```

## Sensitivity to perturbation magnitude (sd)

Primary result uses `sd_web = 0.1` (~10% CV/link). This re-runs the paired ensemble
at sd = 0.1 and 0.2 and reports the fraction of webs where cod recovers more *without*
the seal increase. Expensive (two full ensembles) — `eval=FALSE`; set TRUE to run.

```{r sd-sensitivity, eval=FALSE}

robustness_at_sd <- function(sd_val, n = n_sims, seed = 42) {
  pr <- run_paired_sims(params, n_sims = n, sd = sd_val,
                        effort_factual = effort_factual,
                        effort_counter = effort_counter, seed = seed)
  ok <- which(!vapply(pr$factual, is.null, logical(1)) &
              !vapply(pr$counter, is.null, logical(1)))
  jc <- match("Atlantic Cod", sppx)
  cod_more <- vapply(ok, function(k)
    term_bio(pr$counter[[k]])[jc] > term_bio(pr$factual[[k]])[jc], logical(1))
  data.frame(sd = sd_val, n_webs = length(ok),
             pct_cod_recovers_more_without_seals = round(100 * mean(cod_more), 1))
}
do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.1, 0.2), robustness_at_sd))

```

## Biomass Figures - make plot of obs and sims

```{r}
# read in biomass and catches data
biomass_ts <- readRDS("Ess_data/biomass_ts.RDS")
biomass_ts <- biomass_ts |> rename(Biomass_Obs = Biomass)

# Extract biomass — convert to plain data frame immediately
sim_bio  <- lapply(sims_counter, function(x) { m <- reshape2::melt(getBiomass(x, min_w = species_params(params)$biomass_cutoff), varnames = c("time","Species"), value.name = "value"); m$time <- as.numeric(as.character(m$time)); m })
sim_bio2 <- lapply(sims_factual,  function(x) { m <- reshape2::melt(getBiomass(x, min_w = species_params(params)$biomass_cutoff), varnames = c("time","Species"), value.name = "value"); m$time <- as.numeric(as.character(m$time)); m })

# Stack all sims and add sim index
df_sim_bio  <- do.call(rbind, sim_bio)
df_sim_bio2 <- do.call(rbind, sim_bio2)

df_sim_bio$sim  <- rep(seq_along(sim_bio),  each = 893)
df_sim_bio2$sim <- rep(seq_along(sim_bio2), each = 893)

# Rename columns
df_sim_bio  <- df_sim_bio  |> rename(Year = time, Biomass = value)
df_sim_bio2 <- df_sim_bio2 |> rename(Year = time, Biomass = value)

# Summarise Scenario 1 (counterfactual)
sim_mean  <- df_sim_bio  |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
              summarise(Biomass = median(Biomass), .groups = "drop")
sim_lower <- df_sim_bio  |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
             summarise(Biomass = min(Biomass), .groups = "drop")
sim_upper <- df_sim_bio  |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
             summarise(Biomass = max(Biomass), .groups = "drop")

# Summarise Scenario 2 (factual)
sim_mean2  <- df_sim_bio2 |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
              summarise(Biomass = median(Biomass), .groups = "drop")
sim_lower2 <- df_sim_bio2 |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
              summarise(Biomass = min(Biomass), .groups = "drop")
sim_upper2 <- df_sim_bio2 |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
              summarise(Biomass = max(Biomass), .groups = "drop")

# Create scenario 1 data frame and join with observed
sim1 <- data.frame(
  Species   = sim_mean$Species,
  Year      = sim_mean$Year,
  sim_mean  = sim_mean$Biomass,
  sim_lower = sim_lower$Biomass,
  sim_upper = sim_upper$Biomass,
  scen      = rep("Scen1", length(sim_mean$Biomass)))

sim1 <- left_join(biomass_ts, sim1)

# Create scenario 2 data frame and join with observed
sim2 <- data.frame(
  Species   = sim_mean2$Species,
  Year      = sim_mean2$Year,
  sim_mean  = sim_mean2$Biomass,
  sim_lower = sim_lower2$Biomass,
  sim_upper = sim_upper2$Biomass,
  scen      = rep("Scen2", length(sim_mean2$Biomass)))

sim2 <- left_join(biomass_ts, sim2)

# Combine both scenarios
time_series <- rbind(sim1, sim2)
time_series <- time_series |> rename(Biomass = Biomass_Obs)

# Add calibration label for years before 1986
time_series <- time_series |> mutate(scen = ifelse(Year < 1986, "Calibration", scen))

# Whole time series, no calibration/scenario split: both scenarios (with their ensemble
# envelopes) run across 1978-2024; they coincide early and diverge as seals increase.

# Define species names and set factor levels
species <- levels(time_series$Species) <- c(
  "Atlantic Cod", "Haddock", "White Hake", "Red Hake", "Silver Hake", "Pollock",
  "Redfish Unseparated", "American Plaice", "Yellowtail Flounder", "Witch Flounder",
  "Atlantic Herring", "Capelin", "Thorny Skate", "Winter Skate", "Spiny Dogfish", 
  "Monkfish", "Sand Lance", "Longhorn Sculpin", "Atlantic Halibut")

# Order species by maximum body weight
maxw <- species_params(params)$w_max
species_df <- data.frame(species, maxw)
species_ordered <- species_df[order(species_df$maxw), "species"]

# Reorder species in the plot from small to large max body size
time_series <- time_series |> arrange(Species) |> mutate(Species = factor(Species, species))
time_series <- time_series |> rename(Scenario = scen)

biomass_plot <- ggplot(time_series,
    aes(x = Year, y = Biomass/1e9, colour = Scenario, fill = Scenario)) +
  facet_wrap(~factor(Species, levels = c(
    "Atlantic Cod", "Haddock", "White Hake", "Red Hake", "Silver Hake", "Pollock",
    "Redfish Unseparated", "American Plaice", "Yellowtail Flounder", "Witch Flounder",
    "Atlantic Herring", "Capelin", "Thorny Skate", "Winter Skate", "Spiny Dogfish",
    "Monkfish", "Sand Lance", "Longhorn Sculpin", "Atlantic Halibut")),
    scales = "free") +
  geom_point(data = filter(time_series, Biomass > 0), colour = "black", size = 0.5) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = sim_lower/1e9, ymax = sim_upper/1e9), alpha = 0.4, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sim_mean/1e9)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1985, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  scale_colour_manual(name   = NULL, values = c("grey70", "#4575B4", "#D73027"),
    labels = c("Reference period",
               "Counterfactual (seals constant)",
               "Factual (seals increasing)")) +
  scale_fill_manual(name   = NULL, values = c("grey70", "#4575B4", "#D73027"),
    labels = c("Reference period", 
               "Counterfactual (seals constant)",
               "Factual (seals increasing)")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4),
                      labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(y = "Biomass (kt)", x = "Year") +
  theme_pubr() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
   legend.text     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.title.x    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x     = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 0.8))
ggsave(filename = paste0(save_dir, "biomass_plot.jpeg"), plot = biomass_plot,
       width = 13, height = 8.5, units = "in", dpi = 400)

biomass_plot
```


Taylor plot and correlation plot
```{r}
library(openair)
time_series_first4 <- sim2[, 1:4]
colnames(time_series_first4) <- c("Year", "Species","Biomass_observed", "Biomass")
time_series_first4<- time_series_first4 %>%  filter(Year >= 1986, Year <= 2024)
modStats(time_series_first4,
         obs  = "Biomass_observed", mod  = "Biomass",type = "Species",rank = "Species")

taylor_data <- time_series_first4 %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  mutate(Biomass_observed_norm = Biomass_observed / mean(Biomass_observed, na.rm = TRUE),
  Biomass_norm          = Biomass / mean(Biomass_observed, na.rm = TRUE) ) %>% ungroup()

# Choose distinct colors for species

x = TaylorDiagram(
  taylor_data,obs = "Biomass_observed_norm", mod = "Biomass_norm", group= "Species")


# Correlation plot by Species
ggplot(time_series_first4,
       aes(x = Biomass_observed, y = Biomass)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Species), size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  stat_cor(
    method = "pearson",
    label.x.npc = "left",
    label.y.npc = 0.95,
    size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs( x = "Observed biomass", y = "Model biomass")

```


Figure for CATCHES 
```{r}
# read in observed catch data
yield_ts <- readRDS("Ess_data/yield_ts.RDS")
yield_ts <- yield_ts |> rename(Yield_Obs = Yield) |>
  filter(!Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")) |>
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = unique(Species))) |>
  arrange(match(Species, levels(Species)), Year)

# ============================================================
# Function to extract catches from a simulation
# ============================================================
trimYield <- function(sim) {
  plotYieldGear(sim, return_data = TRUE) |>
    filter(Gear %in% Gear) |>
    filter(!Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")) |>
    group_by(Year, Species) |>
    summarise(Yield = sum(Yield), .groups = "drop")
}

# ============================================================
# Extract catches from all simulations
# ============================================================
sim_catches  <- lapply(sims_counter, trimYield)
sim_catches2 <- lapply(sims_factual, trimYield)

# Add simulation IDs
for (i in seq_along(sim_catches))  sim_catches[[i]]$sim  <- i
for (i in seq_along(sim_catches2)) sim_catches2[[i]]$sim <- i

# ============================================================
# Combine simulation outputs
# ============================================================
df_sim_catch  <- do.call(rbind, sim_catches)
df_sim_catch2 <- do.call(rbind, sim_catches2)

# ============================================================
# Scenario 1 summaries
# ============================================================
sim_mean_c  <- df_sim_catch |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
               summarise(Yield = median(Yield), .groups = "drop")
sim_lower_c <- df_sim_catch |> group_by(Species, Year) |>    
                summarise(Yield = min(Yield), .groups = "drop")
sim_upper_c <- df_sim_catch |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
                summarise(Yield = max(Yield),  .groups = "drop")

# ============================================================
# Scenario 2 summaries
# ============================================================
sim_mean2_c  <- df_sim_catch2 |> group_by(Species, Year) |>
                 summarise(Yield = median(Yield), .groups = "drop")
sim_lower2_c <- df_sim_catch2 |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
                summarise(Yield = min(Yield),  .groups = "drop")
sim_upper2_c <- df_sim_catch2 |> group_by(Species, Year) |> 
                 summarise(Yield = max(Yield),  .groups = "drop")

# ============================================================
# Create scenario data frames
# ============================================================
sim1_c <- data.frame(
  Species   = sim_mean_c$Species,
  Year      = sim_mean_c$Year,
  sim_mean  = sim_mean_c$Yield,
  sim_lower = sim_lower_c$Yield,
  sim_upper = sim_upper_c$Yield,
  scen      = "Scen1")

sim1_c <- right_join(yield_ts, sim1_c, by = c("Species", "Year"))

sim2_c <- data.frame(
  Species   = sim_mean2_c$Species,
  Year      = sim_mean2_c$Year,
  sim_mean  = sim_mean2_c$Yield,
  sim_lower = sim_lower2_c$Yield,
  sim_upper = sim_upper2_c$Yield,
  scen      = "Scen2")

sim2_c <- right_join(yield_ts, sim2_c, by = c("Species", "Year"))

# ============================================================
# Combine scenarios
# ============================================================
time_series_c <- rbind(sim1_c, sim2_c)
time_series_c <- time_series_c |> mutate(scen = ifelse(Year < 1986, "Calibration", scen))|> 
                rename(Yield = Yield_Obs)
```

## Modelled fishing yield (Bottom Trawl, Fixed Gear, Small Mesh, Pelagic gears; seal predation excluded) vs. observed catch, by species, 1978–2024. Ribbon shows ensemble uncertainty; points show observed landings.
```{r}
# ============================================================
# SETUP — Required data and function definitions
# ============================================================

# Gear types included in "Commercial Fisheries" (excludes Seals)
gear <- c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Small_Mesh", "Pelagic")

# Function: extract commercial fishing catches only (excludes Seals)
trimYield <- function(sim) {
  plotYieldGear(sim, return_data = TRUE) |>
    filter(Gear %in% gear) |>
    filter(!Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")) |>
    group_by(Year, Species) |>
    summarise(Yield = sum(Yield), .groups = "drop")
}

# Function: extract seal predation removals only
trimSealYield <- function(sim) {
  plotYieldGear(sim, return_data = TRUE) |>
    filter(Gear == "Seals") |>
    filter(!Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")) |>
    group_by(Year, Species) |>
    summarise(Yield = sum(Yield), .groups = "drop")
}

# Observed catch data (for optional comparison against modelled output)
yield_ts <- readRDS("Ess_data/yield_ts.RDS")
yield_ts <- yield_ts |>
  rename(Yield_Obs = Yield) |>
  filter(!Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")) |>
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, levels = unique(Species))) |>
  arrange(match(Species, levels(Species)), Year)


# ============================================================
# Gear-based catch summary (excludes Seals) — COUNTERFACTUAL only
# ============================================================
sim_catches_gear_C <- lapply(sims_counter, trimYield)

for (i in seq_along(sim_catches_gear_C)) sim_catches_gear_C[[i]]$sim <- i
df_gear_C <- do.call(rbind, sim_catches_gear_C)

gear_mean_C  <- df_gear_C |> group_by(Species, Year) |> summarise(Yield = median(Yield), .groups = "drop")
gear_lower_C <- df_gear_C |> group_by(Species, Year) |> summarise(Yield = min(Yield),    .groups = "drop")
gear_upper_C <- df_gear_C |> group_by(Species, Year) |> summarise(Yield = max(Yield),    .groups = "drop")

gear_summary_C <- data.frame(
  Species   = gear_mean_C$Species,
  Year      = gear_mean_C$Year,
  sim_mean  = gear_mean_C$Yield,
  sim_lower = gear_lower_C$Yield,
  sim_upper = gear_upper_C$Yield,
  type      = "Commercial Fisheries"
)

# ============================================================
# Seal predation catch summary — COUNTERFACTUAL only
# ============================================================
sim_catches_seal_C <- lapply(sims_counter, trimSealYield)

for (i in seq_along(sim_catches_seal_C)) sim_catches_seal_C[[i]]$sim <- i
df_seal_C <- do.call(rbind, sim_catches_seal_C)

seal_mean_C  <- df_seal_C |> group_by(Species, Year) |> summarise(Yield = median(Yield), .groups = "drop")
seal_lower_C <- df_seal_C |> group_by(Species, Year) |> summarise(Yield = min(Yield),    .groups = "drop")
seal_upper_C <- df_seal_C |> group_by(Species, Year) |> summarise(Yield = max(Yield),    .groups = "drop")

# ============================================================
```

# Compare size-based trophic cascades under each scenario relative to histrorical when cod were abundant across species
```{r}
# Extract reference spectra from historical period — 1985 as representative pre-change year
spectra_reference <- plotSpectra(sims_counter[[1]], return_data = TRUE, time_range = 1978:1985)

# Extract spectra for Scenario 1 (with constant predation) for 1995–2010
spectra_scen1 <- plotSpectra(sims_counter[[1]], return_data = TRUE, time_range = 2015:2024)

# Extract spectra for Scenario 2 (with increasing seal predation) for 1995–2010
spectra_scen2 <- plotSpectra(sims_factual[[1]], return_data = TRUE, time_range = 2015:2024)


# Join Scenario 1 spectra with reference and calculate symmetric relative difference
sf1 <- left_join(spectra_reference, spectra_scen1, by = c("w", "Legend")) |>
  mutate(rel_diff = (`value.y` - `value.x`) /
                    (`value.x` + `value.y`))

# Join Scenario 2 spectra with reference and calculate symmetric relative difference
sf2 <- left_join(spectra_reference, spectra_scen2, by = c("w", "Legend")) |>
  mutate(rel_diff = (`value.y` - `value.x`) /
                    (`value.x` + `value.y`))

# Add scenario labels for plotting

  
sf1$scenario <- "Counterfactual (seals constant)"
sf2$scenario <-  "Factual (seals increasing)"

sf1$scenario <- "Counterfactual (seals constant)"
sf2$scenario <- "Factual (seals increasing)"

# Combine both scenarios into one data frame
combined_data <- rbind(sf1, sf2)


# Define manual colors for the scenarios
linecolours <- c("#4575B4", "#D73027")

# Define manual colors for the scenarios (named so order can't flip factual/counterfactual)
linecolours <- c("Factual (seals increasing)" = "#D73027", "Counterfactual (seals constant)" = "#4575B4")

# Set factor levels for consistent facet ordering
combined_data$Legend <- factor(combined_data$Legend,
  levels = c("Resource", "Atlantic Cod", "Haddock", "White Hake", "Red Hake", "Silver Hake",
             "Pollock", "Redfish Unseparated", "American Plaice", "Yellowtail Flounder",
             "Witch Flounder", "Atlantic Herring", "Capelin", "Thorny Skate",
             "Winter Skate", "Spiny Dogfish", "Monkfish", "Sand Lance",
             "Longhorn Sculpin", "Atlantic Halibut"))

# Create the trophic cascade plot
trophic_cascades_plot <- ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = w, y = rel_diff, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~Legend, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Weight (g)", y = "Symmetric relative difference") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = linecolours) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 1, colour = "dark grey", linewidth = 0.75) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

# Save the plot to file
ggsave(filename = paste0(save_dir, "trophic_cascades_plot.jpeg"),
  plot = trophic_cascades_plot, width = 11, height = 7.5, units = "in", dpi = 400)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Shared styling helper so both plots look identical except for the data
style_spectra <- function(p, title) {
  p +
    scale_x_log10(labels = scales::trans_format("log10", scales::math_format(10^.x))) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = scales::trans_format("log10", scales::math_format(10^.x))) +

      text = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),

      legend.title = element_blank(),
      legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0.1, "cm"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 1.2),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,size = 18) ) +

}
```

Spectra_community
Data Prep
```{r}
stat <- read.csv("Ess_data/LF_Biomass_Abund.csv")

# Survey COMMON_NAME -> mizer species lookup (defined in 01; needed here for bio_size)
species_code_lookup <- c(
  "COD(ATLANTIC)"             = "Atlantic Cod",
  "HADDOCK"                   = "Haddock",
  "WHITE HAKE"                = "White Hake",
  "SILVER HAKE"               = "Silver Hake",
  "POLLOCK"                   = "Pollock",
  "REDFISH UNSEPARATED"       = "Redfish Unseparated",
  "AMERICAN PLAICE"           = "American Plaice",
  "YELLOWTAIL FLOUNDER"       = "Yellowtail Flounder",
  "SPINY DOGFISH"             = "Spiny Dogfish",
  "HALIBUT(ATLANTIC)"         = "Atlantic Halibut",
  "SQUIRREL OR RED HAKE"      = "Red Hake",
  "MONKFISH,GOOSEFISH,ANGLER" = "Monkfish",
  "NORTHERN SAND LANCE"       = "Sand Lance",
  "WITCH FLOUNDER"            = "Witch Flounder",
  "HERRING(ATLANTIC)"         = "Atlantic Herring",
  "THORNY SKATE"              = "Thorny Skate",
  "WINTER SKATE"              = "Winter Skate",
  "LONGHORN SCULPIN"          = "Longhorn Sculpin",
  "CAPELIN"                   = "Capelin")

# species vector (defined later at ~1309 in the original; needed here for ab_lookup)
sp <- species_params(params)$species

# Full-range bio_size (1978–2024), built from stat
bio_size <- stat |>
  mutate(strat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(STRAT)))) |>
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466) |>
  filter(YEAR >= 1978, YEAR <= 2024) |>
  select(Year = YEAR, species_name_raw = COMMON_NAME,
         length_cm = FLEN, Biomass = Biomass_Strata_KG) |>
  mutate(
    # Herring FLEN is recorded in mm (all rows) — convert to cm to match other species
    length_cm = ifelse(species_name_raw == "HERRING(ATLANTIC)", length_cm / 10, length_cm),
    Species = species_code_lookup[species_name_raw]) |>
  filter(!is.na(Species)) |>
  select(Year, Species, length_cm, Biomass)

# Per-species a/b lookup, joined by Species (NOT the mizer weight-grid vector `w`)
ab_lookup <- tibble(
  Species = sp,
  a = species_params(params)$a,
  b = species_params(params)$b)

# COMMUNITY-level consistently-sampled size window: the weight classes the survey samples in
# >= 75% of years POOLED across all species (a single contiguous range, so the community
# spectrum stays smooth rather than per-species jagged). Same >= 75% principle as the
# per-species mean-weight window in 04, applied at the community level here because this is a
# community aggregate. Restricting BOTH observed and modelled community spectra to it keeps
# model and observed treated the same way. Single source of truth: Ess_data/make_size_windows.R.
comm_win <- read.csv("Ess_data/community_size_window.csv")

# Restrict the observed community spectrum to the community-level consistently-sampled window
bio_size <- bio_size |>
  left_join(ab_lookup, by = "Species") |>
  group_by(Species) |>
  mutate(w = a * length_cm^b) |>
  filter(!is.na(Biomass), w >= comm_win$wlo, w <= comm_win$whi) |>   # community window
  ungroup()

# Log-spaced weight-class bins: breaks, midpoints, and widths must all align (12 bins)
breaks <- 10^seq(0, 6, 0.5)
mid    <- sqrt(breaks[-length(breaks)] * breaks[-1])   # geometric midpoint of each log-spaced bin
widths <- diff(breaks)     # width of each bin

bio_size$weightclass <- cut(bio_size$w, breaks = breaks)
levels(bio_size$weightclass) <- mid
bio_size$weightclass <- round(as.numeric(as.character(bio_size$weightclass)), 2)

bio_size$widths <- cut(bio_size$w, breaks = breaks)
levels(bio_size$widths) <- widths
bio_size$widths <- round(as.numeric(as.character(bio_size$widths)), 2)

# Biomass_Strata_KG is in kilograms; the model (and 01's biomass_obs) is in grams.
# Convert kg -> g (* 1e3) so the observed size-spectrum overlay is on the same units as the model.
bio_size$norm_biomass <- bio_size$Biomass * 1e3 / bio_size$widths
```

```{r}
# Size spectra of the observed 
# bio_size <- read.csv("Ess_data/bio_size.csv")   # match the name used below
biomass_size_spectra <- bio_size %>%
  group_by(weightclass, Year) %>% 
  summarise(nbiomass = sum(norm_biomass)) %>%
  ungroup() 

#Observed Reference period 1970-1985
mean_biomass_size_spectra_ref <- biomass_size_spectra  %>% 
  filter(Year<1986)%>%
  group_by(weightclass) %>% 
  summarise(mean_nbiomass=mean(nbiomass))
#Observed final decade 2015-2024 (matches the modelled scenario window 2015:2024)
mean_biomass_size_spectra_post <- biomass_size_spectra  %>%
  filter(Year>=2015)%>%
  group_by(weightclass) %>%
  summarise(mean_nbiomass=mean(nbiomass))

# create function to calculate *community* size spectrum from a time period.
# Restricted to the COMMUNITY-level consistently-sampled window [comm_win$wlo, comm_win$whi]
# (the same size range as the observed community spectrum), so model and observed span the
# same sizes without the jaggedness that per-species windows introduce at the community level.
sizespec <- function(sim, time_range) {
  plotSpectra(sim, power = 1, resource = FALSE, return_data = TRUE, time_range = time_range) |>
    filter(w >= comm_win$wlo, w <= comm_win$whi) |>   # community window
    group_by(w) |>
    summarise(value = sum(value), .groups = "drop")
}


ssdf_ref   <- lapply(sims_counter, sizespec, time_range = 1978:1985)
ssdf_scen1 <- lapply(sims_counter, sizespec, time_range = 2015:2024)
ssdf_scen2 <- lapply(sims_factual, sizespec, time_range = 2015:2024)

# Add simulation ID to each element in the list
iter <- length(ssdf_ref)

for (i in 1:iter) {
  ssdf_ref[[i]]$sim   <- i
  ssdf_scen1[[i]]$sim <- i
  ssdf_scen2[[i]]$sim <- i
}

# Combine all the size spectra sims dataframes into one data frame for each scenario
df_ssdf_ref <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, ssdf_ref)
df_ssdf_1   <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, ssdf_scen1)
df_ssdf_2   <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, ssdf_scen2)

# Compute summary statistics (median, 10th, 90th percentile) for REFERENCE
df_ssdf_ref_mean  <- df_ssdf_ref |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = median(value), .groups = "drop")
df_ssdf_ref_lower <- df_ssdf_ref |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = min(value), .groups = "drop")
df_ssdf_ref_upper <- df_ssdf_ref |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = max(value), .groups = "drop")

# Compute summary statistics for Scenario 1
sim_mean1_ssdf  <- df_ssdf_1 |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = median(value), .groups = "drop")
sim_lower1_ssdf <- df_ssdf_1 |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = min(value), .groups = "drop")
sim_upper1_ssdf <- df_ssdf_1 |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = max(value), .groups = "drop")

# Compute summary statistics for Scenario 2
sim_mean2_ssdf  <- df_ssdf_2 |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = median(value), .groups = "drop")
sim_lower2_ssdf <- df_ssdf_2 |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = min(value), .groups = "drop")
sim_upper2_ssdf <- df_ssdf_2 |> group_by(w) |> summarise(N = max(value), .groups = "drop")

# Create summary dataframe for REFERENCE
ss_c_ref <- data.frame(
  w          = df_ssdf_ref_mean$w,
  sim_meanN  = df_ssdf_ref_mean$N,
  sim_lowerN = df_ssdf_ref_lower$N,
  sim_upperN = df_ssdf_ref_upper$N,
  scen       = rep("REF", length(df_ssdf_ref_mean$w)))

# Create summary dataframe for Scenario 1
ss_c_1 <- data.frame(
  w          = sim_mean1_ssdf$w,
  sim_meanN  = sim_mean1_ssdf$N,
  sim_lowerN = sim_lower1_ssdf$N,
  sim_upperN = sim_upper1_ssdf$N,

# Create summary dataframe for Scenario 2
ss_c_2 <- data.frame(

  scen       = rep("Scen2", length(sim_mean2_ssdf$w)))

# Combine all scenarios
time_series_ss <- rbind(ss_c_1, ss_c_2, ss_c_ref)
sf1$scenario <- "Counterfactual (seals constant)"
sf2$scenario <- "Factual (seals increasing)"

# Recode scenario names
time_series_ss <- time_series_ss %>%
  mutate(scen = recode(scen,
    "Scen1" = "Counterfactual (seals constant)",

# Define line colours
linecolours <- c(

# Define axis limits for annotation

# Create the spectra plot

  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = sim_lowerN, ymax = sim_upperN), alpha = 0.1, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
```

Relative difference spectra of Sceanrio 1 and 2 with reference

```{r}
library(ggtext)
# Join Scenario 1 spectra with reference and calculate symmetric relative difference
sf1 <- left_join(ss_c_ref, ss_c_1,by = "w") %>%
  mutate(rel_diff = (sim_meanN.y - sim_meanN.x) / (sim_meanN.x + sim_meanN.y))

# Join Scenario 2 spectra with reference and calculate symmetric relative difference
sf2 <- left_join(ss_c_ref, ss_c_2,by = "w") %>%
  mutate(rel_diff = (sim_meanN.y - sim_meanN.x) / (sim_meanN.x + sim_meanN.y))
# -----------------------------
# 2. Add scenario labels
# -----------------------------
ss_c_ref <- ss_c_ref %>%mutate(scenario = "Reference period")
ss_c_1 <- ss_c_1 %>%mutate(scenario = "Counterfactual (seals constant)")
ss_c_2 <- ss_c_2 %>%mutate(scenario = "Factual (seals increasing)")

# -----------------------------
# 3. Ensure consistent column names
# -----------------------------
# Rename numeric columns to a common base name for relative difference calculation
ss_c_ref <- ss_c_ref %>%rename(value = sim_meanN)
ss_c_1 <- ss_c_1 %>%rename(value = sim_meanN)
ss_c_2 <- ss_c_2 %>% rename(value = sim_meanN)

# -----------------------------
# 4. Compute relative differences between reference and each scenario
# -----------------------------
sf1 <- ss_c_ref %>%left_join(ss_c_1, by = "w", suffix = c(".ref", ".scen1")) %>%
  mutate(rel_diff = (value.scen1 - value.ref) / (value.scen1 + value.ref),
         scenario = "Counterfactual (seals constant)")

sf2 <- ss_c_ref %>%left_join(ss_c_2, by = "w", suffix = c(".ref", ".scen2")) %>%
  mutate(rel_diff = (value.scen2 - value.ref) / (value.scen2 + value.ref),
         scenario = "Factual (seals increasing)")


# 5. Combine both scenarios
# -----------------------------
combined_data <- bind_rows(sf1, sf2)

# -----------------------------
# 5b. OBSERVED symmetric relative difference, computed the SAME WAY as the model curves above:
#     (recent - reference)/(recent + reference), with the SAME periods as the model
#     (reference = 1978-1985, recent = 2015-2024; the survey starts in 1978 so `Year < 1986`
#     is the 1978-1985 reference). Units cancel in the ratio, so it is directly comparable.
#     The real world had INCREASING seals, so this observed shift is the empirical analogue of
#     the FACTUAL (red) curve.
# -----------------------------
obs_reldiff <- full_join(mean_biomass_size_spectra_ref, mean_biomass_size_spectra_post,
                         by = "weightclass", suffix = c(".ref", ".post")) |>
  mutate(rel_diff = (mean_nbiomass.post - mean_nbiomass.ref) /
                    (mean_nbiomass.post + mean_nbiomass.ref)) |>
  filter(is.finite(rel_diff))

# -----------------------------
# 6. Define manual colors for the scenarios
# -----------------------------
linecolours <- c(
"Counterfactual (seals constant)" = "#4575B4",
"Factual (seals increasing)" = "#D73027")

# -----------------------------
# 6b. Ensemble envelope for the relative-difference curves.
#     Compute rel_diff PER food web (paired within web: each web's own 2015-24 spectrum vs
#     its OWN 1978-85 reference), then take the 10-90% spread across the 1000 webs at each
#     size. 10-90% matches the manuscript ribbon convention (design note above).
# -----------------------------
rd_env <- bind_rows(
  df_ssdf_ref |> rename(ref = value) |>
    inner_join(df_ssdf_1 |> rename(s = value), by = c("w", "sim")) |>
    mutate(rel_diff = (s - ref) / (s + ref),
           scenario = "Counterfactual (seals constant)"),
  df_ssdf_ref |> rename(ref = value) |>
    inner_join(df_ssdf_2 |> rename(s = value), by = c("w", "sim")) |>
    mutate(rel_diff = (s - ref) / (s + ref),
           scenario = "Factual (seals increasing)")
) |>
  group_by(scenario, w) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(rel_diff, 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi = quantile(rel_diff, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# -----------------------------
# 7. Plot
# Define y-axis limits for annotation (you can also use ggplot_build to get them dynamically)
y_limits <- range(c(combined_data$rel_diff, rd_env$lo, rd_env$hi), na.rm = TRUE)

Relative_trophic_plot <-  ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = w, y = rel_diff, colour = scenario)) +
  # 10-90% ensemble envelope (per-web paired rel_diff), drawn under the median lines
  geom_ribbon(data = rd_env, aes(x = w, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = scenario),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = linecolours, guide = "none") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) + labs(x = "Size (g)", y = "Symmetric relative difference") +
  scale_x_log10(limits = c(comm_win$wlo, comm_win$whi),           # SAME x-axis as panel (a)
                breaks = c(1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000),
                labels = c("1", "10", "100", "1000", "10000")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = linecolours) +
  # Observed symmetric relative difference (survey post vs reference). Defined in the figure
  # caption rather than the legend; filled diamond to match the observed points in panel (a).
  geom_point(data = obs_reldiff, aes(x = weightclass, y = rel_diff),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.0, shape = 23, fill = "black", colour = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkgrey", linewidth = 0.75) +
  annotate( "text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = "(b)",
    hjust = -0.5, vjust = 1.5, fontface = "bold", size = 6) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),  # match panel (a)
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

Relative_trophic_plot
spectra = spectra_plot/Relative_trophic_plot #bind plots

ggsave(filename = paste0(save_dir, "spectra_plot.jpeg"), plot = spectra, width = 11, height = 7.5, units = "in", dpi =400)
```

## Diagnostic (not for manuscript) — baseline reorganization vs the seal signal

Internal triage only, `eval=FALSE` — NOT a paper figure. Held at constant 1978 effort
the Stage-2 model still reorganizes substantially (groundfish decline, forage release),
confirming the hindcast is an intentional transient relaxation, not an equilibrium run.
Useful for spotting which per-species excursions are mechanism vs anomaly; the seal
attribution itself rests on the paired factual − counterfactual difference above, which
cancels the reorganization common to both scenarios. Run by hand when needed.

```{r appendix-baseline-vs-seal, eval=FALSE}
# Three deterministic (un-randomised) projections from the SAME calibrated 1978 state:
#   control        = ALL gears frozen at 1978 (no forcing change) -> the baseline
#                    reorganization intrinsic to the off-equilibrium Stage-2 parameters
#   factual        = observed fishing + seal increase 1978->2024
#   counterfactual = observed fishing + seals frozen at 1978
# The factual/counterfactual SEPARATION is the seal signal; both ride on top of the
# large shared baseline drift that the control characterises.
effort_const1978    <- effort_factual
effort_const1978[]  <- matrix(effort_factual[1, ], nrow(effort_factual),
                              ncol(effort_factual), byrow = TRUE)
sim_ctrl <- project(params, effort = effort_const1978)
sim_cf0  <- project(params, effort = effort_counter)   # deterministic counterfactual

# Per-species biomass above each species' survey cutoff (Halibut also gets its upper
# cutoff as its model w_max exceeds the survey's max caught size).
w <- params@w; dw <- params@dw; sp <- params@species_params$species
cl <- params@species_params$biomass_cutoff; cl[is.na(cl)] <- 0
ch <- params@species_params$biomass_cutoffHigh
bmass <- function(sim) {
  yrs <- as.integer(dimnames(sim@n)[[1]])
  m <- matrix(NA_real_, length(yrs), length(sp), dimnames = list(yrs, sp))
  for (j in seq_along(sp)) {
    hi  <- if (sp[j] == "Atlantic Halibut" && !is.na(ch[j])) ch[j] else Inf
    idx <- w >= cl[j] & w <= hi
    m[, j] <- rowSums(sweep(sim@n[, j, idx, drop = FALSE], 3, w[idx] * dw[idx], "*"))
  }
  m
}

# Ratio to each species' own 1978 value (1.0 = no change from the start state).
runs <- list("constant 1978 effort"        = sim_ctrl,
             "counterfactual (seals 1978)" = sim_cf0,
             "factual (seal increase)"     = sim0)
ratio_df <- imap_dfr(runs, function(s, nm) {
  m <- bmass(s)
  as.data.frame(sweep(m, 2, m["1978", ], "/")) |>
    rownames_to_column("Year") |> mutate(Run = nm)
}) |>
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year), Run = factor(Run, levels = names(runs))) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(Year, Run), names_to = "Species", values_to = "ratio")

drift_plot <- ggplot(ratio_df, aes(Year, ratio, colour = Run)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("constant 1978 effort"        = "grey50",
                                 "counterfactual (seals 1978)" = "#2c7fb8",
                                 "factual (seal increase)"     = "firebrick")) +
  labs(y = expression(B(t) / B[1978]), x = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())
ggsave(paste0(save_dir, "appendix_baseline_vs_seal.jpeg"), drift_plot,
       width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 200)
drift_plot

```
